Yes. You didn't name a topic, so I looked up three companies from your list that look like a good match for us and that you haven't added yet.

**DEFY MEDICAL, LLC (best fit)**
- A telehealth clinic in Tampa, FL. It offers testosterone and other hormone therapy, peptides, weight-loss plans and virtual primary care.
- That's the hormone and peptide market we're aiming at, and close to what MyWellness App does.
- Patients pay cash. One review says lab work can sometimes be claimed on insurance, so they likely deal with a lot of lab results, which our AI can read.
- Their app launched about a year ago and is rated 1.4★, so they may be open to a better one.
- Websites disagree on when it was founded (2011, 2013 or 2016) and on its prices, so check those before you reach out.

**Primestin Care, LLC (good fit)**
- A membership primary-care service with a telehealth app. Members get 24/7 access to providers, virtual urgent care and prescription refills.
- It's sold through Zion HealthShare, where members can add it for $5–10 a month. That means its app has to work across that whole membership base.
- Their app is rated 2.2★, with only 17 ratings.

**Ritch's Pharmacy (weaker fit)**
- An independent community pharmacy in Mountain Brook, Alabama. It offers refill syncing, pill packaging and home delivery.
- I couldn't confirm that it does compounding. A business called "Ritch's Vital Care" in Birmingham, AL does infusion and nutrition, but I couldn't tell whether the two are connected.
- It's a small pharmacy, so it may not be able to pay $8 per member per month.
